PullRequest.Title: agentHost: preserve late MCP ownership decisions and provenance
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #345015. Follow-up to merged #344961.

Addresses all three outstanding review findings:

- [Scoped decisions lost during late ownership adoption](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/344961#discussion_r4412719527): move explicit unowned host Global/Workspace decisions through the enablement service before resolving the owned target. Preserve existing destination decisions, pending replacements, and the stable Session ID; do not persist inherited SDK defaults.
- [Conflicting plugin identity ignored](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/344961#discussion_r4412719612): use known runtime `sourcePlugin` in every late-discovery matching path, retaining ambiguity checks.
- [Stale plugin metadata after provenance changes](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/344961#discussion_r4412719666): discard incompatible discovery metadata, defaults, and source navigation while preserving unrelated metadata, connection state, and live identity. A newly confirmed SDK default still takes effect immediately when switching plugins.

This does not migrate legacy client plugin state, change client-provided plugin forwarding, or depend on the separate SDK plugin-lifecycle work.

Review follow-up in `1f2af0b39ba`: restrict workspace adoption to the resolved session workspace, defer it during initialization/directory resolution, and merge pending writes per scope with persisted/queued destination precedence. Preserve full-replacement clears and nonconflicting Session writes. Retain fallback plugin names in both controller adoption and publication merging. Added 13 regression tests, including pre-fix reproductions of all three review findings on this PR.

### Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed.
- The following focused Electron unit-test command — **488 passed**:

  ```sh
  ./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot \
    --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/shared/mcpCustomizationController.test.ts \
    --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostCustomizationEnablementService.test.ts \
    --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/shared/customizationEnablementGate.test.ts \
    --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts \
    --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts \
    --grep 'McpCustomizationController|CustomizationEnablement|discovered SDK customizations|MCP|mcp'
  ```

- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `git diff --name-only -z -- '*.ts' | xargs -0 npm run eslint --` — passed for all 16 changed TypeScript files before the initial commit; rerun passed for all four TypeScript files modified by the review fixes.
- `git diff --check` — passed; commit hygiene hooks also passed.

Coverage includes real-service Global/Workspace/Session disablement through late Copilot discovery, Global/Workspace persistence across service recreation, destination precedence, pending initialization, no SDK-default persistence, change notifications, conflicting and disambiguated plugin identities, and repeated provenance updates to user/workspace/builtin/another plugin.

Limits: no live-provider UI scenario, full integration suite, or Windows/Linux run. The initial full `Build Fast` workspace task failed in unrelated extension compilation (including missing `EditorModel.renderWhitespace` in the Markdown editor); the client-only build and client typecheck above passed. Some mocked CLI subprocesses emitted read-only log-directory warnings; all selected tests passed.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed per-server call, synchronous all-session notification path, non-coalescing downstream queue, and filesystem/IPC boundaries are all explicit in the call graph. Exact user session/server counts vary, so magnitude is uncertain, but the multiplicative mechanism and realistic trigger are direct.
Findings.PerformanceResource: per-session customization filesystem scans and SDK IPC calls
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For D late-discovered MCP servers with migrated global decisions and S loaded sessions, this loop emits D all-session change events, causing O(D×S) queued customization recomputations; active Copilot sessions additionally issue D serialized mcp.listConfigured RPCs each.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated background filesystem/SDK work increases discovery latency and I/O/IPC load, especially with multiple open sessions and multiple servers in one plugin discovery result.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The same discovery merge only projected the discovered child and updated ownership metadata; it did not mutate enablement storage or trigger cross-session customization refresh/reconciliation work.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Late plugin discovery now migrates each matching server independently and immediately notifies all affected sessions after each migration, rather than treating the discovery result as one state transition.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added call at line 10607 runs inside the loop over every live MCP server. Each successful global migration synchronously calls _notifyDecisionChanged; _getAffectedSessions treats a global key move as affecting every session. Before this diff, this loop performed no ownership migration and emitted no enablement refreshes.
Findings.Title: Batch ownership adoptions before refreshing every session
Findings.Impact: When a plugin exposes several runtime-first MCP servers that have explicit global enablement decisions, one discovery refresh schedules multiple full customization republishes for every loaded session. AgentSideEffects appends each refresh to a per-session promise chain without coalescing; Claude republishes perform four filesystem discovery scans (and may query the SDK), while each active Copilot session independently performs an mcp.listConfigured RPC per event.
Findings.Evidence: The added call is inside `for (const server of live?.customizations ?? [])`. `adoptMcpServerOwnership` immediately invokes `_notifyDecisionChanged`; moving the global key makes `_getAffectedSessions` enumerate every `getSessionUris()` entry for both source and destination snapshots. `AgentSideEffects._publishSessionCustomizationsSoon` chains every event onto the prior promise, so D events are not collapsed, and `_publishSessionCustomizations` calls `agent.getChatCustomizations` each time. `ClaudeAgentSession.getSessionCustomizations` performs parallel multi-root/rules/MCP/hooks filesystem scans, and `CopilotAgentSession` reacts to every matching event by running `_reconcileMcpServerEnablement`, whose first boundary is `session.rpc.mcp.listConfigured()`.
Findings.Recommendation: Apply all ownership moves from one discovery result in a single service transaction (or defer/coalesce enablement notifications for the current turn): migrate decisions synchronously so later resolution sees them, but persist once and emit one unioned session-change event after the loop. Preserve immediate single-server behavior where batching is unavailable.

Scenarios.Scenario: Late Copilot SDK plugin discovery adopts ownership for runtime-first MCP servers with existing host decisions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The discovery result is merged synchronously in SessionPluginController._resolveCustomizationEnablement; each ownership move and enablement resolution completes before publication can return. Persistence is scheduled asynchronously, while change listeners synchronously enqueue downstream republish/reconcile work off the immediate return path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and schedule persistence of migrated global/workspace decisions and LRU state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Called once per adoption that moves a persisted decision; multiple calls in one turn share the storage throttler, which bounds actual writes but does not coalesce downstream notifications.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Discovery projection did not mutate enablement storage, so it scheduled no persistence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Scheduling and serialization occur synchronously; the atomic filesystem write completes asynchronously and is not required before discovery publication progresses.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover multi-root customizations, rules, MCP servers, and hooks from disk.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four parallel scan groups per queued refresh per affected Claude session; D adoption notifications queue D complete refreshes for each such session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Late Copilot ownership discovery emitted no global enablement events, so it did not trigger these cross-provider rescans.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the initiating discovery return path, but each queued session republish waits for all scans and consumes filesystem/CPU resources across sessions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Call the SDK session RPC mcp.listConfigured, followed by enable/disable RPCs only if resolved state differs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least one listConfigured RPC per adoption event per active affected Copilot session; the per-session sequencer serializes D calls but does not collapse them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The discovery merge did not emit enablement-change events and therefore did not invoke this reconciliation path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the initiating publication path, but serialized RPCs delay completion of subsequent MCP reconciliation work and contend with the active SDK session.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: D matching MCP servers in the discovery result, S loaded session states, and A active provider sessions. Global decisions make every session affected, producing D×S customization refreshes and D×A provider reconciliations without batching.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Adoptions run serially in the server loop. Storage writes use a shared throttler, but enablement notifications are emitted independently. AgentSideEffects serializes refreshes per session without coalescing and runs different sessions concurrently; each Copilot session serializes its RPC reconciliations, while Claude performs four scans in parallel per queued refresh.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: SDK discovery and session customization state may already be warm, but the notification queue still invokes getChatCustomizations for every event. The final equality check can avoid an unchanged state dispatch only after filesystem/SDK work has completed. Ownership metadata prevents normal later status updates from re-adopting the same published server.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added call is in a per-server loop; global key movement enumerates all session URIs; consumers queue rather than coalesce each event; filesystem scans and RPC calls are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneously loaded sessions and plugin MCP servers varies, and storage throttling reduces physical file writes. The D×S recomputation and D×A RPC mechanism is nevertheless explicit and occurs for the PR's targeted global-decision migration scenario.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity missing-coalescing regression: batch ownership moves or at least union/defer notifications so one discovery result produces one refresh per affected session.

Scenarios.Scenario: Deferred ownership adoption while session metadata or worktree directory resolution is pending
Scenarios.CriticalPath: adoptMcpServerOwnership records an in-memory pending entry and returns. Session initialization or a working-directory event later resolves the workspace, applies ownership before queued replacements, persists migrated decisions, and notifies affected sessions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read session metadata from the session state store before resolving session-scoped enablement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One memoized read per initialized session, independent of P pending adoptions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Session initialization already read this metadata; the diff adds pending ownership replay after the existing read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initialization waits for this read; ownership replay follows it synchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist migrated global/workspace decisions after pending resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per pending adoption that actually moves persistent state; storage writes are throttled globally.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Queued replacements could persist decisions, but ownership migration itself did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialization/scheduling is synchronous, physical write asynchronous.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Immediately flush session metadata when replaying a queued session-scope replacement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Depends on queued replacements, not ownership alone; ownership can redirect a pending replacement but does not add a write when no replacement exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Pending replacement replay already performed this session metadata write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Write is asynchronous and tracked for whenIdle; replay does not await it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P pending server targets for one session, plus the service-wide pending-map size. Keys deduplicate repeated adoption for the same session and unowned persistent key.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Session enablement loading is memoized by _sessionLoads. Replay runs synchronously when that load or directory transition completes; pending replacements and adoptions are applied serially for the session.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Pending ownership is a keyed overwrite cache and entries are deleted after resolution. Session loads are memoized. A permanently pending worktree can retain its entries for the service lifetime, but the diff does not establish realistic unbounded creation independent of already retained session state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for deferred replay behavior and boundary counts; low for any harmful retention magnitude.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A worktree could remain pending for an extended period, but no evidence shows high-cardinality abandoned sessions or a lost cleanup boundary beyond pre-existing service-retained session maps.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: pending entries deduplicate by target and are consumed on the existing initialization/directory-resolution transitions; no concrete unbounded-retention regression is proven.

Scenarios.Scenario: Runtime provenance changes invalidate incompatible plugin discovery metadata and defaults
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Runtime inventory/provenance refresh rebuilds top-level MCP customizations in memory, removes incompatible discovery metadata, resolves enablement, and emits a replacement action only when the customization changed.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of live MCP servers times the number of published customization entries searched for a matching declaration; effective server inventories are typically small and the diff adds only constant metadata checks to the pre-existing scans.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Updates execute synchronously inside controller transactions; observable runtime-state publication is coalesced by the transaction.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Published customization metadata and the live map serve as the warm state. Once incompatible metadata is removed or the correct plugin identity is attached, subsequent unchanged updates compare equal and avoid replacement actions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed path consists of in-memory map/list scans and small object copies.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Inventory size varies, but no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary is reached by the changed metadata checks themselves.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the added provenance checks do not materially change the existing scan complexity or introduce a costly boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 17 changed files and all diff pages. Submitted one medium-confidence/high-mechanism-confidence finding for unbatched per-server ownership notifications causing D×S filesystem recomputation and D×A SDK RPC fanout; pending replay and provenance invalidation introduced no other concrete regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
